doc: The Claude Code CLI's own names. The SDK emits no in-process telemetry; the CLI it spawns self-instruments, so these are the CLI's vocabulary.

carriers.doc: The turns and tool results handed to the model, tagged in-band - only those new since the previous request of the same thread, so the request's earlier messages are on that thread's earlier requests.
The whole system instruction, reported beside the conversation: a detached request frame.
The system prompt, reported beside the conversation: a detached request frame.

The client's environment block: a system turn the client appends after the conversation's newest input. A snapshot, because a resumed process reports the reminders of the turns before it beside its own, so a later reminder may restate an earlier one; but within one value each position is a reminder of its own, as `system_reminders_count` states, so two identical ones are two. Not a detached frame, because it follows the inputs of its request rather than preceding them.
The tool a span was asked to run, alongside its input.

detect.doc: The CLI subprocess emits every span under one prefix. Two service names because the CLI reports one and the host process wrapping it reports the other.
detect.label: ClaudeAgentSDK

request_threads.doc: A request exports what is new since the previous request of its thread, not the request it sent: the turns in `new_context`, the reminders in `system_reminders`. The thread is the session and the agent: `query_source` is `sdk` for the main agent and names a subagent, which also states its own `agent_id`. A log-only capture states neither, which is one thread per session.

messages.doc: The whole system instruction the client sent, not only the caller's part: its billing header and the SDK's own preamble, then the caller's prompt, each a block of its own, joined by a blank line. The caller's prompt is the last block and may hold blank lines itself, so the split stops after two. Where `user_system_prompt` carries that prompt whole, the rule reading it shows it and the section is skipped. The attribute is a preview, cut at 500 characters on a subagent, and a cut block is not what the model was told: the length the CLI states beside it is a JavaScript string length, so it counts UTF-16 units.

routes.doc: Every block of the instruction is the system's.

messages.doc: The caller-supplied system prompt, emitted once per session rather than per request. Blank counts as absent here: this dialect writes the attribute whether or not there is a prompt.

The reminders of a subagent's request whose delta opens its user turn - the request that hands the subagent its task. The client sends every reminder but the last inside that turn, each a text part of its own wrapped in `<system-reminder>` tags, and only the last - the environment block - as the system turn it appends; the attribute exports them unwrapped, in order, joined by a rule. Only a subagent's: a main-agent request that resumes a process restates the earlier turns' reminders beside its own, and those are the system turns they were (`claude-code/multi_turn`). Read before the rule below, which then owns nothing here.

routes.doc: A reminder before the last: a part of the user turn, as the client sent it.

wrap_text.because: The CLI wraps a reminder it puts into a user turn as `<system-reminder>\n${text}\n</system-reminder>` (the native `claude` binary of @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64 0.3.284, function `XLr`, closing tag constant `Ms`), and every captured request part carrying the tag - 10 of 10 across the Claude Code family's model-requests.json - is exactly a section of its span's `system_reminders` inside that wrapper.

routes.doc: The last reminder: the environment block, a system turn of its own.

messages.doc: The environment block the client appends to the request as a system turn of its own: the working directory, the platform, the tools' context. Part of what the model was told, carried whole rather than as a preview, so it is read as the system message it is.

routes.doc: Several reminders are joined by a rule, as `system_reminders_count` says; each is a system turn of its own.

messages.doc: Either side of the conversation, in one attribute, distinguished by a bracketed tag - and several sections joined by a separator, one per parallel tool call, each read on its own so every result keeps its own id.

routes.doc: A tool result. The tag's remainder is the call id, which is what pairs the result with its tool_use block rather than leaving it to be guessed from content. The name-tagged form is the same result as raw structured telemetry, so it is dropped - narrowly: only when the capture lacks the id prefix *and* the body opens as JSON, so if that prefix changes an unrecognised section still reaches the feed unlinked instead of vanishing.
Anything else is the user's turn - including an unrecognised tag, which is read rather than discarded.

messages.doc: A tool call rebuilt from the tool span. The read carrier is the tool's *name*, which becomes the block's name member; the input is attached from another attribute where the payload sits under a bracketed tag naming the tool, so it is stripped before parsing - parsing without stripping fails and the member would silently fall back to its empty form. An unparseable input does fall back to `{}`, because the block's shape requires the member.

message_events.name: tool.output
message_events.doc: The CLI's tool result body, emitted only with tool-content logging enabled. A container: `claude-code.tool_output` reads the member that holds the output, so the event's other members (the path, the command) are not reported as a message too.

event_roles.name: tool.output
event_roles.doc: This dialect's CLI writes a tool result body on its own span event rather than on a convention event, so the name is the only thing that says the message is a tool's answer. Needs `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT=1`.
